attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: A faithful retrospective observation: roughly a decade of synthetic-data use for driverless cars has not solved the problem. The normalised wording keeps the approximate duration and adds no causal claim.

contract.note: Reading 'solved' as reliable general driverless operation, not a bounded service, is an ordinary, fair reading of firm language. The result depends on that reading because the speaker gave no scope or threshold.

evidence.note: A dated 2016 ECCV paper trains road-scene segmentation on game-generated synthetic images. This supports about nine years of use by May 2025. It says nothing about whether driving was solved.
Waymo's own May 2025 disclosure of driverless service in four cities. It shows bounded commercial operation, not general autonomy, and is not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: The duration part is supported by the 2016 paper. The packet has no admissible independent evidence on whether general driverless operation was still unsolved by 2025-05-22. The key operational-limits documents could not be read, and Waymo's disclosure is context only. The core 'hardly solved' part is therefore not settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, repeated twice in his post.

semantics.note: A categorical causal claim that imminent-AGI narratives speed up the AI race. The paragraph before it says such projects are 'probably' having this effect, but the quoted sentence itself is unhedged and repeated, so it is treated as a firm commitment.

contract.note: The plain reading (net causal acceleration of investment, development or policy support by the post date) is fair and ordinary. Requiring causal or decision-record evidence is appropriate.

evidence.note: The AI 2027 authors' statement of their aim. Their intent neither establishes nor rules out the effect Marcus alleges.
A June 2025 congressional letter using race framing. It is dated after the post and attributes no decision to AGI-imminence narratives.

reviews.rationale: No evidence in the packet isolates a causal effect of imminent-AGI narratives on the AI race by 2025-05-22, or measures acceleration against slowing. Both items are context only. The evidence available does not settle the causal claim.
